description: WHAT HAPPENED ON THE SITE — the GA4 Data API report, and the tool that answers "where is our traffic coming from", "which campaign converted", "which landing page is working". Pass metrics by name (activeUsers, sessions, screenPageViews, conversions, totalRevenue, engagementRate, bounceRate, averageSessionDuration …) and dimensions to break them down by (sessionDefaultChannelGroup, sessionSource / sessionMedium / sessionCampaignName, landingPage, pagePath, country, deviceCategory, date, eventName …). GA4 publishes hundreds of both and each property ships its OWN custom dimensions, so names are forwarded as given rather than validated against a copied list — use list_analytics_definitions to see a property's custom ones. THE PROPERTY IS A NUMERIC ID (e.g. 123456789), NOT the G-XXXXXXX Measurement ID — run list_analytics_properties to resolve it. Dates default to the last 28 days and accept either YYYY-MM-DD or GA4's relative forms ("28daysAgo", "yesterday", "today"). PERIOD OVER PERIOD IN ONE CALL: compare:"previous_period" (or "previous_year") adds the earlier period and returns per-period totals plus `change` (absolute + %) computed from GA4's own totals — quote it, never redo the maths; or pass up to 4 named dateRanges. comparisons put segments side by side; totals:true adds a total row. Rows come back as flat named objects. When GA4 says the data is SAMPLED, TRUNCATED, rolled into an "(other)" row or thresholded, completenessNotes says so in words; repeat those when reporting. Read-only, 0 credits.

aggregations.description: extra summary rows over the result: TOTAL, MINIMUM, MAXIMUM or COUNT

compare.description: also read the period before startDate–endDate (or the same dates a year earlier) and return `change`

comparisons.description: segments side by side: [{name, dimensionFilter}] or [{comparison:"comparisons/123"}]; adds a comparison column

comparison.description: saved GA4 comparison id such as comparisons/1234; use instead of name and dimensionFilter

dimensionFilter.description: FilterExpression selecting this segment, same shape as dimensionFilter

name.description: label for this segment; becomes the value of the comparison column

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR — default the property currency

dateRanges.description: up to 4 periods instead of startDate/endDate; rows gain a dateRange column; with two, change = the FIRST relative to the SECOND

name.description: label for this period, shown in the dateRange column

startDate.description: period start, YYYY-MM-DD or a GA4 relative date such as 28daysAgo

dimensionFilter.description: NARROW THE REPORT — a GA4 FilterExpression, exactly one of andGroup | orGroup | notExpression | filter. Without it a report is the WHOLE property. Example: {"filter":{"fieldName":"sessionSource","stringFilter":{"matchType":"EXACT","value":"google"}}}; combine with {"andGroup":{"expressions":[…]}}. METRICS CANNOT BE USED HERE — use metricFilter.

dimensions.description: GA4 dimension names to break the metrics down by — omit for a single total row

keepEmptyRows.description: true = keep rows whose metrics are all zero

limit.description: rows to return, 1–250000 (default 50). 250,000 is GOOGLE's per-request maximum, not ours — asking for more is silently capped there.

metricFilter.description: Filter the AGGREGATED rows, GA4's having-clause — same FilterExpression shape. Example: {"filter":{"fieldName":"sessions","numericFilter":{"operation":"GREATER_THAN","value":{"int64Value":"30"}}}}. DIMENSIONS CANNOT BE USED HERE — use dimensionFilter.

offset.description: skip this many rows — how you page past `limit`. Use the nextOffset the previous call returns.

dimension.description: dimension to sort by; use instead of metric

metric.description: metric to sort by; use instead of dimension

orderType.description: dimension sort order: ALPHANUMERIC, CASE_INSENSITIVE_ALPHANUMERIC or NUMERIC

orderByMetric.description: sort by this metric — must be one of the metrics requested

orderDesc.description: default true (largest first) when orderByMetric is set

property.description: the NUMERIC GA4 property id from list_analytics_properties (e.g. "123456789") — never the G-XXXXXXX Measurement ID, and it must be one SHARED with this profile

startDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD or a GA4 relative date like "28daysAgo" (default 28daysAgo)

name: analytics_report
title: Run a GA4 report
